newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Oakland airport details expansion plans.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Oakland airport details expansion plans.

text.p: The Oakland International Airport on Wednesday detailed an expansion programme to accommodate anticipated growth in passenger and cargo volume.

The airport released environmental documents for a group of 18 projects which would enable the airport to handle about 13.8 million passengers annually by 2000, compared with last year's figure of 9.8 million.
Expanded cargo facilities would allow the airport to handle an antipated one million tons in 2000, against last year's 541,000 tons, the airport said.

The release of the environmental impact report and the environmental impact statement begins a 60-day public comment period. During this period, the Port of Oakland, the owner and operator of the airport, and the Federal Aviation Administration must respond to public opinion on the possible impact of the project on the community and the environment.
The Port of Oakland said it hoped to certify the Environmental Impact Report in March 1997, after which construction can begin on several road improvement projects.

The Port said it expected the FAA to issue a decision by June 1997, allowing construction to begin on such projects as the expansion of the terminals and air cargo facilities, development of new parking facilities and improvement of access roads.
